title: Coalitional influence toward an output
statement: Let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$, let $J$ be a set of coordinates, and let $b\in\{−1,1\}$. The coalitional influence of $J$ toward $b$ is the probability that the coalition can achieve output $b$, minus the probability that a uniformly random input already has output $b$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
$J$ is a finite set of coordinates
caveat: The formal snippet uses coalitionSuccessProbability but does not provide its definition, so the probability being subtracted cannot be characterized more precisely from the supplied statement.
